48970-across-texas.title: Across Texas
48970-across-texas.creator: Unknown
48970-across-texas.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. ed by his stirring experience in the mountainous forests of Maine. He was naturally strong and active, and one glance at his bright eyes, his ruddy cheeks, and his alert movements told his sister Nellie and the beloved father and mother that the prescription of the physician had worked like a charm.

arxiv-2101-00552.title: Hyponormal dual Toeplitz operators on the orthogonal complement of the Harmonic Bergman space
arxiv-2101-00552.creator: Chongchao Wang 1, Xianfeng Zhao 2
arxiv-2101-00552.description: Abstract . In this paper, we mainly study the hyponormality of dual Toeplitz operators on the orthogonal complement of the harmonic Bergman space. First we show that the dual Toeplitz operator with bounded symbol is hyponormal if and only if it is normal.

arxiv-2105-00035.title: Long-distance quantum key distribution based on the physical loss control
arxiv-2105-00035.creator: N. S. Kirsanov, N. R. Kenbaev, A. B. Sagingalieva, D. A. Kronberg, V. M. Vinokur, G. B. Lesovik Terra Quantum AG, St. Gallerstrasse 16A, CH-9400 Rorschach, Switzerland
arxiv-2105-00035.description: Abstract Existing quantum cryptography is resistant against secrecy-breaking quantum computers but suffers fast decay of the signal at long distances. The various types of repeaters of propagating quantum states have been developed to meet the challenge, but the problem is far from being solved.

arxiv-2206-11644.title: Mass radius and mechanical properties of the proton via strange ϕ \phi meson photoproduction
arxiv-2206-11644.creator: Xiao-Yun Wang, Chen Dong, Quanjin Wang
arxiv-2206-11644.description: Abstract In this work, the cross sections of ϕ \phi photoproduction are systematically investigated with the two gluon exchange model and the pomeron model. The results obtained show that the theoretical values of the two models agree well with the experimental data.

arxiv-2207-08452.title: The early evolution of young massive clusters:
arxiv-2207-08452.creator: M. Stoop, L. Kaper, A. de Koter, D. Guo, H. J. G. L. M. Lamers, S. Rieder
arxiv-2207-08452.description: Abstract Context. Young massive clusters provide the opportunity to study the outcome of the star formation process and the early evolution of star clusters. In the first few million years the (massive) stars dynamically interact, producing runaways and affecting the initial (binary) population. Aims.

arxiv-2306-07750.title: Free Energy of Coupled Oscillators: Lamb Shifts and van der Waals Interactions
arxiv-2306-07750.creator: Peter W. Milonni
arxiv-2306-07750.description: Abstract The Helmholtz free energy of oscillators in thermal equilibrium with electromagnetic radiation is obtained from the Pauli–Hellmann–Feynman theorem and applied to some aspects of Lamb shifts and van der Waals interactions. I Introduction Lamb shifts and van der Waals interactions may be attributed to the coupling of atoms to the zero-point electromagnetic field.

arxiv-2412-13737.title: On the Compression of Language Models for Code: An Empirical Study on CodeBERT
arxiv-2412-13737.creator: Giordano d’Aloisio, Luca Traini, Federica Sarro, Antinisca Di Marco
arxiv-2412-13737.description: Abstract Language models have proven successful across a wide range of software engineering tasks, but their significant computational costs often hinder their practical adoption. To address this challenge, researchers have begun applying various compression strategies to improve the efficiency of language models for code.

arxiv-2502-03899.title: A Slicing Model for Transport Networks with Traffic Burst Control and QoS Compliance for Traffic Flows
arxiv-2502-03899.creator: Aitor Encinas-Alonso 1, Carlos M. Lentisco 1, Ignacio Soto 1, Luis Bellido 1, David Fernandez 1
arxiv-2502-03899.description: Abstract Network slicing has emerged as a key network technology, providing network operators with the means to offer virtual networks to vertical users over a single physical network infrastructure. Recent research has resulted mainly in techniques for managing and deploying network slices, but the implementation of network slices on a real physical transport network infrastructure has received much less attention.

arxiv-2505-11374.title: A magnetic field detection in the massive O-type bright giant 63 Oph Facilities: ADS, ASAS-SN, CFHT (ESPaDOnS), Gaia, Kepler, MAST, Mercator1.2m (HERMES), Max Planck:2.2m (FEROS), NOT (FIES)
arxiv-2505-11374.creator: James A. Barron, Gregg A. Wade, Gonzalo Holgado, Sergio Simón-Díaz
arxiv-2505-11374.description: Abstract Surface magnetic fields are detected in less than 10 % 10\% of the massive O-type star population and even less frequently among ‘old’ massive stars approaching the terminal-age main sequence (TAMS). It is unclear to what extent the rarity of magnetic detections in massive stars near the TAMS is due to magnetic field decay or observational biases.

arxiv-2508-20533.title: Extensive entanglement between coupled Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids in and out of equilibrium
arxiv-2508-20533.creator: Taufiq Murtadho, Marek Gluza, Nelly H. Y. Ng
arxiv-2508-20533.description: Abstract Quantum entanglement exists in nature but is absent in classical physics, hence it fundamentally distinguishes quantum from classical theories. While entanglement is routinely observed for few-body systems, it is significantly more challenging to witness in quantum many-body systems. Here, we theoretically study entanglement between two parallel and spatially separated Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids (TLLs) partitioned along the longitudinal axis.

arxiv-2509-23937.title: Diffusion Models are Kelly Gamblers
arxiv-2509-23937.creator: Akhil Premkumar
arxiv-2509-23937.description: Abstract We draw a connection between diffusion models and the Kelly criterion for maximizing returns in betting games. We find that conditional diffusion models store additional information to bind the signal X X with the conditioning information Y Y , equal to the mutual information between them.

arxiv-2511-15346.title: Comprehensive Assessment of Th 3 + \mathrm{Th}^{3+} Properties for Nuclear Clock and Fundamental Physics Applications
arxiv-2511-15346.creator: A. Chakraborty, B. K. Sahoo
arxiv-2511-15346.description: Abstract By employing singles, doubles, and triples excitations within the relativistic coupled-cluster framework, we perform comprehensive calculations of a wide range of atomic properties for the Th 3+ ion. These properties are essential for advancing nuclear clock technology and probing fundamental physics.

arxiv-2602-05436.title: Lipschitz regularity of harmonic quasiconformal maps between Lyapunov domains in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n}
arxiv-2602-05436.creator: Anton Gjokaj, David Kalaj
arxiv-2602-05436.description: Abstract . We prove that every sense-preserving harmonic K K –quasiconformal homeomorphism f : D → Ω f\colon D\to\Omega between Lyapunov domains (equivalently, bounded C 1 , α C^{1,\alpha} domains) in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} , α ∈ ( 0 , 1 ] \alpha\in(0,1] , is globally Lipschitz on D ¯ \overline{D} .

openalex-w7215847507.creator: Luciane Pimentel Corrêa Campos, Marcelo Augusto Machado Vasconcelos, Lourival Dias Campos
openalex-w7215847507.description: This article aims to present an experience report on the implementation of suspended gardens using PET bottles in municipal schools in Capanema-PA, Brazil, in collaboration with the Municipal Secretariat of Environment (SEMMA) and the Municipal Secretariat of Education (SEMED)....

pmc-10557515.title: A non-linear optimization based robust attribute weighting model for the two-class classification problems
pmc-10557515.creator: Adi Alhudhaif
pmc-10557515.description: BackgroundThis article aims to determine the coefficients that will reduce the in-class distance and increase the distance between the classes, collecting the data around the cluster centers with meta-heuristic optimization algorithms, thus increasing the classification performance.MethodsThe proposed mathematical model is based on simple mathematical calculations, and this model is the fitness function of optimization algorithms.

pmc-11356605.title: Retrospective Study of Factors Affecting the Accuracy of Predicting Vancomycin Concentrations in Patients Aged 75 Years and Above
pmc-11356605.creator: Masaki Takigawa, Hiroyuki Tanaka, Masako Kinoshita, Toshihiro Ishii, Masayuki Masuda, Maija Dambrova
pmc-11356605.description: Background and Objectives: The predicted serum concentrations of vancomycin are determined using population pharmacokinetic parameters. However, the accuracy of predicting vancomycin serum concentrations in the older population remains unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the accuracy of predicting vancomycin serum concentrations and identifying elements that diminish the prediction accuracy in older people.

pmc-11522640.title: Evaluation of pesticide contamination risks and sustainable practices in Ecuadorian agriculture
pmc-11522640.creator: Angelica Geovanna Zea Cobos, Yaroslava Robles Bykbaev, Fredi Portila Farfán, Pablo Caballero Perez
pmc-11522640.description: Pesticide use is crucial in global agriculture to control pests and increase crop yields. In Ecuador, the use of pesticides, including fungicides and insecticides, is common in crops such as potatoes and tomatoes. However, the indiscriminate use of these products has proven to have negative consequences for human health and the environment.

pmc-11606162.title: Impact of IL-17A Inhibitors on Serum Uric Acid Levels in Psoriatic Patients with Hyperuricemia: A Prospective Observational Study
pmc-11606162.creator: Chao Wu, Chunxia He, Haimeng Wang, Wenming Wang, Hongzhong Jin
pmc-11606162.description: PurposeThis prospective observational study investigated whether interleukin (IL)-17A inhibitors could reduce serum uric acid (SUA) levels in psoriatic patients with hyperuricemia. It also explored the risk factors for hyperuricemia in psoriatic patients and the effectiveness of IL-17A inhibitors for the skin lesions of psoriatic patients with hyperuricemia.

pmc-12793902.title: Role of adult attachment and spiritual attachment on meaning in life among religious minorities in Thailand: Insights for mental health promotion
pmc-12793902.creator: Suriwong Wongratanamajcha, Justin DeMaranville, Tinakon Wongpakaran, Unchalee Permsuwan, Shirley Worland
pmc-12793902.description: Attachment theory suggests that secure relationships are foundational to meaning in life, but less is known about the role of spiritual attachment, especially among religious minorities. This study examined whether attachment to God mediates the relationship between insecure human attachment and the presence of meaning in life among Thai Protestant Christians.

pmc-13037618.title: Effect of floor versus conventional elevated housing on the welfareand meat quality of rabbits
pmc-13037618.creator: José Manuel Robles-Robles, Adrián Muñoz-Cuautle, José Luis Ponce-Covarrubias, María Esther Ortega-Cerrilla, Fernando Utrera-Quintana, Ricardo Martínez-Martínez, Abel Villa-Mancera
pmc-13037618.description: Objective:The housing system is a crucial determinant of animal welfare. This study aimed to compare the effects of intensive housing with those of alternative floor housing on the welfare of rabbits and their meat production.Materials and Methods:Eighty New Zealand rabbits (40 females and 40 males) with an initial mean weight of 1.

pmc-13214545.title: Optimizing research publication of nurse researchers through a mentored writing retreat programme (MWRP): A participatory action research protocol
pmc-13214545.creator: Remya U Rajendran, Mamatha Shivananda Pai, Baby S Nayak, Judith Angelitta Noronha, Vimala Ramoo, Srinivas Mutalik, Vasudeva Guddattu, Vishnu Renjith
pmc-13214545.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundNurse researchers often face challenges in publishing their work due to limited writing skills, inadequate mentorship, and insufficient institutional support. Strengthening research dissemination is essential for improving evidence-based practice, professional growth, and the visibility of nursing scholarship.ObjectiveThisprotocol aims to identify barriers and facilitators to research publication among nurse researchers and to evaluate the effectiveness of a Mentored Writing Retreat Programme (MWRP) in optimizing the publication process.MethodsA participatory action research design will be adopted and implemented in two phases.

pmc-13465477.title: Association between enteral nutrition timing and postoperative anion gap trajectory in cardiac surgery ICU patients: a retrospective study based on the MIMIC-IV database
pmc-13465477.creator: Shan-jiao Chen, Jia-wen Lu, Ya-nan Yao, Chao-quan Liu
pmc-13465477.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the association between enteral nutrition (EN) timing and postoperative anion gap (AG) trajectory in ICU patients undergoing cardiac surgery.MethodsData were extracted from the MIMIC-IV database. Cardiac surgery patients receiving EN were classified into preoperative and postoperative groups according to whether EN was first recorded before or after surgery. Baseline comparability was assessed.

pmc-13495896.title: Nanofiber‐Supported Decellularized Matrix Membrane Creates a Biomimetic Biochemical and Biophysical Niche for Intestinal Organoid Epithelium
pmc-13495896.creator: Jaeseung Youn, Hyeonji Kim, Nam Than, Juhyeok Kim, Jangwon Yoon, Dohui Kim, Hyun Jung Kim, Dong Sung Kim
pmc-13495896.description: Reconstructing intestinal organoid‐derived epithelium on porous membranes is a promising strategy for building in vitro intestine models that combine biological complexity with experimental accessibility. A central challenge is designing membranes that reproduce the biochemical and biophysical cues of the native intestinal microenvironment. Here, we report a nanofiber‐supported decellularized extracellular matrix (NaDE) membrane engineered to emulate these key features.
